title: Signal and Echo
premise: Rafael Halloran, a xenolinguist whose mind has drifted so far from human speech that he no longer dreams in it, pilots the long-haul relay between colonies that have gone linguistically silent. When he intercepts a distress call in Vessic — a language extinct for two centuries, and one only he can still parse — he discovers it is not a rescue plea but a forged transmission, designed to keep two hostile fleets believing a third power still watches them. Rafael must sustain and eventually weaponize that lie, recruiting a ragged crew of outcasts who become the family he never had. In the end, exposed before both fleets, he gambles everything on broadcasting the truth in every dead language at once, forcing the fleets to confront what they nearly destroyed — and choosing to stay among the people who learned to hear him.
about_author: Dominic Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. Signal and Echo is their second novel, written in harbor towns across three continents.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. He runs the relay route alone, cataloguing colonies that have stopped transmitting, dreaming each night in languages no human speaks. The emotional beat is loneliness disguised as competence — a man fluent in everything except belonging.

chapters.title: Vessic
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A distress signal arrives in Vessic, extinct for two hundred years; he decodes it and realizes it references events that haven't happened yet. Beat: dread mixed with exhilaration — his exile tongue has come back from the grave.

chapters.title: Dead Men Broadcasting
chapters.summary: Rafael traces the signal to the derelict station Meridian-9 and finds Ilsa Voss, a disgraced fleet archivist who forged the transmission to keep two fleets from open war. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual blackmail and mutual need.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She explains the standoff: the Corvane and Ashen fleets each believe a hidden third power enforces peace, and her forgery is the only thing holding them apart. Beat: vertigo — Rafael learns the scale of the lie he's now inside.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Route
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Rafael recruits three outcasts: pilot Sefu Adeyemi, engineer Tam Okafor-Reyes, and teenage stowaway Juno. Beat: friction becoming tentative warmth — the found family begins assembling itself by accident.

chapters.title: Grammar of Threats
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. To keep the lie alive, he must compose new 'third power' transmissions in flawless Vessic, learning to write threats in a language built for mourning. Beat: moral unease as he discovers he's good at deception.

chapters.title: The Corvane Gambit
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. A Corvane patrol boards them hunting the signal's source; Sefu bluffs them off using Rafael's forged codes. Beat: first real danger survived together, cementing trust through shared risk.

chapters.title: What Juno Heard
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The stowaway secretly records Rafael's transmissions and notices they're addressed to someone — a name in Vessic that means 'child.' Beat: tenderness and intrusion; Juno realizes Rafael is speaking to a daughter lost decades ago.

chapters.title: Meridian Falling
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The Ashen fleet bombards Meridian-9 to erase evidence of the forgery; Ilsa barely escapes, wounded. Beat: grief and guilt — the lie now has a body count, and everyone knows it.

chapters.title: The Translator's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Both fleets offer him sanctuary if he betrays the other side's codes. Beat: temptation laid bare — power offered freely, which is how corruption always introduces itself.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Archive
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She reveals she inherited the forgery from her mother, an archivist who maintained the same lie for forty years. Beat: inheritance as burden — the theme made explicit, family as something you're drafted into.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The forged transmitter is failing; without replacement parts from a Corvane black market, the peace collapses in weeks. Beat: ticking clock installed — time is now visibly running out.

chapters.title: Black Market Tongues
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno talks their way into a smuggler bazaar where dead languages are traded like contraband, securing the parts but leaving a trail. Beat: Juno stepping from passenger to crew member, earning their place.

chapters.title: The Man Who Spoke First
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. A Corvane admiral, Renn Halvard, corners Sefu and reveals he knows the third power is fiction — but wants it kept alive for his own reasons. Beat: the lie grows a second author, and he is more dangerous than ignorance.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finally dreams fully in Vessic and understands the language was never extinct — its last speakers went silent on purpose, refusing to serve as weapons. Beat: revelation reframing everything; silence was a choice, and he is undoing it.

chapters.title: Halvard's Peace
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The admiral plans to let the fleets bleed each other, then rule the ruins under the third-power myth. Beat: cold ambition — power's corruption given a face and a reasonable voice.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Ilsa proposes doubling down on the lie; Rafael insists on ending it; the crew splits. Beat: the found family's first true rupture, love tested against conviction.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Halvard seizes their ship and forces Rafael to transmit the forgery under his control; instead Rafael begins broadcasting the truth in every dead language he knows. Beat: climax — the gamble of a lifetime, spoken in tongues the whole sector thought were gone.

chapters.title: Echoes Answer
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Across both fleets, people who secretly kept the old languages alive begin answering the broadcast; Halvard's authority dissolves as the myth of the third power dies publicly. Beat: catharsis — the silenced finding each other, the lie collapsing into truth.

chapters.title: What the Fleets Saw
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Armistice talks convene with Rafael as translator; Ilsa testifies to her family's forty-year deception and is pardoned for it. Beat: accountability without erasure — inheritance acknowledged, then set down.

chapters.title: A Language With Speakers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael teaches the first Vessic class aboard a rebuilt Meridian-9, Juno among his students; he dreams that night in human words for the first time in years. Beat: quiet restoration — the dreamer returns to himself by giving the language away.

chapters.title: Signal and Echo
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Juno's POV. Years later, Juno runs the long route with the old crew scattered but close, sending Rafael a message in Vessic that simply says 'come home.' Beat: resolution — family as a signal you keep answering, an echo that never quite fades.
